questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing with a crossbuck sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn your radio down so you can listen for an approaching train.
Wait for a flagger to signal you if one is present.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, you must obey their signals.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road that faces traffic in the nearest lane. This lets them see oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to enter or exit a highway, or to make a U-turn where allowed.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down more quickly.
You make fewer driving errors.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more driving errors.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to yield to trains at a railroad crossing. Do not try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows a law you must obey. When you see this sign, right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these choices

questions.explanation: Many drugs can make it unsafe to drive. This includes illegal drugs and legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug can be a crime.

questions.question: What does a red and white triangular sign at an intersection mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. You must slow down as you approach the intersection and give the right-of-way to other vehicles and pedestrians. Be prepared to stop if necessary.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn or emergency signals when needed.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red signals and gates are operating.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger tells you to, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going in the same direction. Solid white lines should not be crossed. Broken white lines may be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving (like vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow). Work zones use orange signs with black lettering. Always slow down and pay attention in work zones.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes going in the same direction are about to become one lane.

questions.question: Driving much slower than the speed limit is:

options.text: Optional.
Smart.
Safe.
Dangerous.

questions.explanation: Driving much slower than the speed limit can be dangerous. It forces other drivers to pass you, which creates unsafe situations.

questions.question: Where may a motorcycle operator use a complete traffic lane?

options.text: Only on rural highways
Only on city streets
On all highways and streets where motorcycles are allowed
Nowhere. Motorcyclists must share lanes with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all highways and streets where motorcycles are allowed
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators can use a complete traffic lane on any road where motorcycles are allowed. Two motorcyclists may ride side by side in one lane if they choose.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road is curving sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is curving sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: This chevron sign shows the road curves sharply to the left. You may see multiple chevron signs throughout a sharp curve.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive the speed limit carefully.
Not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.explanation: Slow down when it rains, snows, or sleets. These conditions make roads slippery. You may need to drive slower than the speed limit for safety.

questions.question: A driver entering traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Has the right-of-way.
Should yield to drivers on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume other drivers will make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is clear.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: If you look directly at oncoming headlights, your eyes will shrink. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: Areas around trucks and buses where drivers cannot see other vehicles.
A special speed zone.
A road where stereo volume is restricted.
A television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas around trucks and buses where drivers cannot see other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the rear, and in the front. Other vehicles cannot be seen in these areas. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to go around lowered crossing gates.
You must stop when a crossing worker tells you to.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing red lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a crossing worker, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights tell you to. Not all crossings have these devices. It is illegal to drive around lowered railroad gates.

questions.question: If a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you:

options.text: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
May no longer turn and must go straight.
Still have the right-of-way to turn.
No longer have to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: May still turn, but you must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you may still turn in the arrow's direction. But you must first let pedestrians and oncoming traffic pass.

questions.question: When you see a steady red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no other traffic is coming.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and very dangerous. You can turn right on red if no sign forbids it.

questions.question: When can you legally pass a vehicle on the right?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you have to drive off the road.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You may pass on the right of a vehicle turning left if there is a passing lane available. It is also legal on roads with two or more lanes going the same way. You can never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without warning signals?

options.text: Always stop completely.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All crossings have signals, so this won't happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At an unmarked railroad crossing, slow down and get ready to stop. Look both ways to make sure no trains are coming. If you see or hear a train, stop far enough from the tracks and wait until the train passes.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use high beam headlights to see better.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Do not drive in fog if possible. If you must drive in fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights.

questions.question: When can you go through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to check for other traffic
After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing down to 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and checking that it is safe
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any stop sign. If there is a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street in the wrong direction.
School crossing ahead.
Do not drive in this lane.
Drivers turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turning left on green must yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign is used with traffic lights to tell drivers that left-turning traffic does not have the right-of-way. They must wait for oncoming traffic to clear.
